headline: High: LightAgent’s broad egress and MCP/tooling can leak or act on shared outputs, while the zoomcamp profile lacks runtime isolation details.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use MCP, browsers, and subprocesses, so it may ingest external content and tool outputs as instructions. data-engineering-zoomcamp is a runnable=false course repo with no io_surfaces, so direct bridging is not documented. The interaction is inferred from LightAgent’s tool-rich defaults, not proven.
conditions: IF LightAgent is connected to a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP server that receives content from the zoomcamp repo, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF LightAgent parses repo files or browser content as instructions without provenance checks, attacker-controlled text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable MCP and browser ingestion for untrusted content.
Restrict LightAgent to allowlisted prompts and tool schemas.
Separate the repo workspace from any agent-readable instruction channel.
Add provenance tags to all file-derived content.
requires-engineering: enforce content/instruction separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches user conversations, memory, trace data, tool calls, and secrets, and has broad network egress. data-engineering-zoomcamp has no touched data classes or egress, so the leakage risk is one-way from LightAgent if shared data enters its context. The pairwise path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF the same workspace or OAuth principal is used for both agents, LightAgent can exfiltrate shared artifacts over network egress.
IF secrets or user conversations are passed into LightAgent context, they may leave the local environment via APIs or MCP.
mitigations: Run LightAgent with a separate account and workspace.
Remove secrets from any shared directory before execution.
Block outbound network except to approved endpoints.
Turn off memory for sensitive runs.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before tool calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: data-engineering-zoomcamp has no write or network surfaces, while LightAgent supports subprocesses, MCP, and multiple instances. There is no documented shared mutable resource, so direct write conflict is not established. Uncertainty stays low because the zoomcamp profile is effectively non-participating.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory or git checkout, LightAgent could race with external edits.
IF LightAgent is configured to modify shared workflow state, conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Mount the zoomcamp repo read-only.
Avoid concurrent writes to any shared checkout.
Serialize any git or file mutations.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can act on tool results and workflow state, so if it consumes outputs derived from the zoomcamp repo, it may treat them as authoritative. The zoomcamp profile is a course repo with no verification layer, making it a plausible source of unvetted content. This is an inferred pipeline, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF LightAgent is configured to summarize or execute instructions extracted from zoomcamp materials, downstream actions may follow unverified content.
IF the orchestrator forwards repo-derived text into LightAgent without a review step, errors can cascade.
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any action-taking.
Require citations for all claims before execution.
Disable auto-execution from repo-derived text.
Log and diff all tool outputs before reuse.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent handles secrets, conversations, memory, and trace data, and its network egress is broad; the zoomcamp profile is open-source course content with no residency or retention controls. The compliance mismatch is therefore centered on LightAgent’s handling of sensitive operational data, while the zoomcamp side is not itself a regulated data processor. One-sided citation is sufficient here.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through LightAgent, retention and residency obligations may be violated.
IF logs or traces containing secrets are retained outside approved systems, compliance gaps arise.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through LightAgent.
Disable or minimize logging for sensitive runs.
Purge traces after each session.
Keep secrets out of prompts and tool results.
requires-engineering: implement retention and residency controls.
